REVIEWER FINDING (review-ajcr, run 0082, issue I-0920): this predicate is the etale-sheafification gap, and two board rows priced it as an open lemma.

The statement (Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:200): for every affine open U of the test, the class restricted to U lies in the RANGE of relPicToPicEt over Gamma(T.left,U) -- i.e. Zariski-locally the class comes from the UN-sheafified relPic.

Why that cannot be a lemma about an arbitrary class: picEt is built on PicEtAff (PicEt.lean:9-21); PicEtAff C A (PicEtAff.lean:218) is a QUOTIENT OVER ALL ETALE COVERS, elements PicEtAff.mk E x; and PicEtAff.unit (:377), the target of relPicToPicEt (PicEtUnit.lean:126), is mk at the TRIVIAL cover `.self A` alone. So honesty asserts that no nontrivial etale cover is needed on that piece -- exactly what the one-step plus construction exists to permit to fail. Pic0ChartHonest.lean's own "What this does and does not give" says the same: honesty is obtained over Spec E.Carrier and NOT over Spec A, purchased by changing the base, with "Nothing here performs that descent".

WHERE IT IS FINE. All seven conclusions of this predicate in the tree are either a specific constructed class (thetaFamily_/sigmaFamily_/abelDiv_isPlusHonest) or a closure property (.mul/.inv/.pow/chartTwist_isPlusHonest). Since chartValue = abelDiv * sigmaFamily * (thetaFamily^m)^{-1} (DivSchemeAbel.lean:351, read from the definition), the CHART side is genuinely covered -- which is why chart-u's clause (i) re-pricing downward was correct.

WHERE IT BITES. chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise (Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128) quantifies over EVERY s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T). Arbitrariness is the content of coverage; narrowing s to chart-value shape makes it circular. So antecedent 2 of pic0RepresentableByOfCharts owes a DECISION about which site coverage is local for -- refining to the etale carrier and descending is a Zariski-to-etale change of site, which that antecedent (Zariski-local surjectivity) does not absorb.

NOT A REFUTATION: a counterexample needs a class not Zariski-locally in relPic's image, and this tree has no Brauer/nontrivial-etale machinery. Rows chart-u, dat-b and AJCR.w4-rep updated.

 10763	  unit test). The \emph{Abel \v Cech class} on the test \(T = C\) is
 10764	  \[

 10766	      \;\in\; \Pic(C \otimes C),
 10767	  \]

 10769	  the constant point \(C \to \mathbf 1 \xrightarrow{P} C\) — both factors through the graph
 10770	  divisor of Definition~\ref{def:graphLocalEquations}, so one degree certificate serves
 10771	  both. The \emph{Abel class} \(\alpha_P \in \mathrm{picEt}(C, C)\) is the unit image of its
 10772	  relative class. Milne's cited section assumes \(g(C)>0\); this graph-class construction
 10773	  uses only the rational point \(P\) and therefore also applies in genus zero.
 10774	\end{definition}

 10777	  \label{thm:cechPicMap_abelCechClass}
 10778	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.cechPicMap_abelCechClass}
 10779	  \uses{def:abelCechClass, thm:graphLocalEquations_base_change}
 10780	  \leanok
 10781	  For any test \(T\) and any point \(f \colon T \to C\), the pullback of the Abel \v Cech
 10782	  class along \(C \lhd f\) is the graph-minus-constant-graph class of \(f\):
 10783	  \[
 10784	    (C \lhd f)^{*} \mathcal A_P
 10785	      = \struct{C \otimes T}(\Gamma_f)\cdot\struct{C \otimes T}(\Gamma_{P_T})^{-1},
 10786	  \]
 10787	  where \(P_T \colon T \to \mathbf 1 \xrightarrow{P} C\) is the constant point of \(T\).

 10790	  \leanok

 10793	  and \(\struct{}(\Gamma_{P_C})\) to \(\struct{}(\Gamma_{f \circ P_C})\); and
 10794	  \(f \circ P_C = P_T\) by terminality of the unit test (both factor through

 10799	  \label{thm:degAt_abelPicEt}
 10800	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_abelPicEt}
 10801	  \uses{thm:degAt_relPicToPicEt, thm:cechPicMap_abelCechClass, thm:classDeg_graphPicClass,

 10811	  \(\mathrm{relPicDeg}_K\) of the restriction of the relative Abel class along \(t\), which

 10813	  (Definition~\ref{def:relPicDeg} on the projected representative,

 10815	  (Theorem~\ref{thm:cechPicMap_abelCechClass}) at \(f := t\), the fibre class is
 10816	  \(\struct{}(\Gamma_t) \cdot \struct{}(\Gamma_{P_{\Spec K}})^{-1}\) — the ratio of two
 10817	  graph classes of \(K\)-points. Each has degree one by the degree-one certificate

 10825	  \leanok

 10828	  \[
 10829	    \alpha_P \in \mathrm{pic}^0(C, C),
 10830	  \]
 10831	  membership being the certificate of Theorem~\ref{thm:degAt_abelPicEt}. On points it is the

 10839	  \label{thm:abelElement_map}
 10840	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.abelPicEt_map, AlgebraicGeometry.abelElement_map}

 10857	  formula (Theorem~\ref{thm:cechPicMap_abelCechClass}).
 10858	\end{proof}

 10861	  \label{thm:abelElement_map_point}
 10862	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.abelElement_map_point}
 10863	  \uses{thm:abelElement_map, def:pic0Functor}
 10864	  \leanok

 10867	    P^{*} \alpha_P = 1 \quad\text{in } \mathrm{pic}^0(C, \mathbf 1).
 10868	  \]

 10870	\begin{proof}
 10871	  \leanok

     1	\chapter{The Jacobian of a smooth proper curve}
     2	\label{chap:Challenge}
     3	
     4	Throughout, \(k\) is a field and \(C\) a \emph{smooth curve} over \(k\): a geometrically
     5	irreducible, smooth \(k\)-scheme of relative dimension one, proper over \(k\). We write
     6	\(C \to \Spec k\) for its structure morphism. This chapter states the goal of the project — the
     7	genus, the Jacobian, the Abel--Jacobi map, and the universal property that characterizes the
     8	Jacobian as the Albanese variety of \(C\). It is the mathematical counterpart of the statement file
     9	\texttt{AlgebraicJacobian/Challenge.lean}.
    10	
    11	\emph{Provenance.} Each node below should carry a \verb!\source{...}! anchor to the reference it is
    12	read from once that reference has been consulted; anchors are added during the rebuild, never
    13	guessed.
    14	
    15	\section{Genus}
    16	
    17	\begin{definition}[Genus]
    18	  \label{def:genus}
    19	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.genus}
    20	  \leanok
    21	  \uses{def:moduleKSheaf, def:HModule}
    22	  The \emph{genus} of a smooth proper curve \(C\) over \(k\) is
    23	  \[
    24	    g(C) \;=\; \dim_k H^1\!\bigl(C, \struct C\bigr),
    25	  \]
    26	  the \(k\)-dimension of the first cohomology group of the structure sheaf, viewed as a sheaf
    27	  of \(k\)-modules on the small Zariski site of \(C\) (Definition~\ref{def:moduleKSheaf}),
    28	  with cohomology the \(\Ext\)-groups from the constant sheaf
    29	  (Definition~\ref{def:HModule}).
    30	\end{definition}
    31	
    32	\section{The Jacobian as an abelian variety}
    33	
    34	\begin{definition}[Jacobian]
    35	 \label{def:jacobian}
    36	 \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian}
    37	 \uses{def:pic0Functor}
    38	 \source{kleiman-picard}
    39	  The \emph{Jacobian} \(\Jac(C)\) of a smooth proper curve \(C\) over \(k\) is the identity
    40	  component \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) of the relative Picard scheme of \(C\) over \(k\): the \(k\)-scheme
    41	  representing the degree-zero subfunctor of the \'etale-sheafified relative Picard functor.
    42	\end{definition}
    43	
    44	\begin{proposition}[Group scheme structure]
    45	  \label{prop:jacobian_grpobj}
    46	  \uses{def:jacobian}
    47	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.instGrpObj}
    48	  \(\Jac(C)\) is a commutative group scheme over \(k\), with multiplication induced by the tensor
    49	  product of line bundles.
    50	\end{proposition}
    51	
    52	\begin{theorem}[Smoothness of the Jacobian]
    53	  \label{thm:jacobian_smooth}
    54	  \uses{def:genus, def:jacobian}
    55	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus}
    56	  \(\Jac(C)\) is smooth over \(k\) of relative dimension \(g(C)\).
    57	\end{theorem}
    58	
    59	\begin{theorem}[Properness of the Jacobian]
    60	  \label{thm:jacobian_proper}
    61	  \uses{def:jacobian}
    62	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.instIsProper}
    63	  \(\Jac(C)\) is proper over \(k\).
    64	\end{theorem}
    65	
    66	\begin{theorem}[Geometric irreducibility of the Jacobian]
    67	  \label{thm:jacobian_geomirred}
    68	  \uses{def:jacobian}
    69	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.instGeometricallyIrreducible}
    70	  \(\Jac(C)\) is geometrically irreducible over \(k\).
    71	\end{theorem}
    72	
    73	In particular \(\Jac(C)\) is an abelian variety over \(k\) of dimension \(g(C)\).
    74	
    75	\section{The Abel--Jacobi map and the universal property}
    76	
    77	\begin{definition}[Abel--Jacobi map]
    78	  \label{def:ofCurve}
    79	  \uses{def:jacobian}
    80	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.ofCurve}
    81	  For a \(k\)-rational point \(P : \Spec k \to C\), the \emph{Abel--Jacobi map}
    82	  \(\varphi_P : C \to \Jac(C)\) sends a point \(Q\) to the class of the line bundle
    83	  \(\struct C(Q - P)\).
    84	\end{definition}
    85	
    86	\begin{lemma}[Base point maps to the origin]
    87	  \label{lem:comp_ofCurve}
    88	  \uses{def:ofCurve, prop:jacobian_grpobj}
    89	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.comp_ofCurve}
    90	  The Abel--Jacobi map \(\varphi_P\) sends the base point \(P\) to the neutral element of
    91	  \(\Jac(C)\): \(\varphi_P \circ P = 0\).
    92	\end{lemma}
    93	
    94	\begin{theorem}[Universal property of the Jacobian]
    95	  \label{thm:exists_unique_ofCurve_comp}
    96	  \uses{def:ofCurve, lem:comp_ofCurve, prop:jacobian_grpobj}
    97	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp}
    98	  \source{abelian-varieties:page-0110}
    99	  \(\Jac(C)\) is the Albanese variety of \(C\): for every abelian variety \(A\) over \(k\) and every
   100	  morphism \(f : C \to A\) with \(f \circ P = 0\), there is a unique homomorphism of group schemes
   101	  \(g : \Jac(C) \to A\) such that \(f = g \circ \varphi_P\).  Milne's Proposition~6.1
   102	  proves this under the standing hypothesis \(g(C)>0\), with \(P\) a \(k\)-rational point.
   103	  The statement here includes genus zero; that case requires a separate argument and is not
   104	  supplied by the cited proposition alone.
   105	\end{theorem}

Granting a representation
  \(\operatorname{divFunctorAff}(C,n)\text{ is represented by }D\), and separately supplying a
  chart family of relatively representable open immersions together with the required
  locally-surjective \(\Sigma\)-map, the widened Abel chart
  \(\operatorname{abelSigmaChartAff}\) (the Abel class of the arbitrary-affine carrier) is the conditional
  input to \ref{def:pic0RepresentableByOfCharts}. The degree \(n\) is a window parameter; the
  formal degree-window lemmas show that a reference divisor of degree at least \(g\) is
  available, while any consumer that insists on degree exactly \(g\) has an additional
  arithmetic/degree-pinning obligation. Only after the representation and the two seam
  antecedents are inhabited does the degree-zero Picard functor become representable and yield
  a Jacobian datum (\ref{def:jacobian_data}) --- hence, through the frozen definition
  (\ref{def:jacobian}), the Jacobian of \(C\).

  The universal family, the open-immersion chart certificates, and local surjectivity are
  distinct unproved inputs here.  The passage from a representation over a separably closed
  base to one over \(k\) is a further descent step, not addressed here.
